content.title: About
content.content: The ostrich is a large, flightless bird native to Africa. Ostrich meat is considered a lean, high‑protein option with a mild, slightly sweet flavor that resembles beef.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ostriches can reach heights of up to 2.7 m and weigh over 150 kg.
Ostrich eggs are the largest of any bird; one egg weighs about 1.4 kg.
In the wild, ostriches can run up to 70 km/h.
Ostrich meat contains less fat than beef and almost twice as much iron.
Ostriches are farmed not only for meat but also for feathers, leather, and eggs.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ostrich meat provides about 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with beef, ostrich meat contains only 2–3 % fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: High iron content
items.content: The iron in ostrich meat is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Source of zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Ostrich meat has lower cholesterol levels than most red meats.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to ostrich meat.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Like any raw meat, ostrich can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; proper cooking is essential.

items.title: Higher cost
items.content: Ostrich meat is typically more expensive than conventional meats, which may limit frequent consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ostrich meat can be prepared like beef: pan‑seared, roasted, stewed, or grilled. It pairs well with herbs, spices, wine‑based or tomato sauces. Fillets are often sliced into thin steaks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh ostrich meat in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
